lines.en: : Whaaaaaaaat the fuck is that thing?
: Large and in charge. Let’s bake this bread.
: It’s beautiful...
: Right here’s okay?
: Yeah. That’s the only chair we have.
: Sorry...It’s just been a while since I’ve talked about this.
: Can you start by introducing yourself?
: Yumi Yamaguchi. Professor of psychology at Kumon-mi University.
: Can you tell us your version of what happened that day?
: God...where do I even begin?
: Girls! I present to you — the death ball!
: Can’t...breathe! So...heavy!
: I would like to get off Mr. Bones’ Wild Ride now.
: That...is a very large ball.
: It was such a large ball!
: Do you have an estimation on how large it was exactly?
: Very!
: So, like...what do we do with it?
: Excellent question, Yumi!
: Rika, what do we do with it?
: Me?!
: Yeah! You get to choose the rules of this game.
: Why me?! I can’t be trusted with balls this big. Besides, you won’t even let me drive your car! It’s proof I can’t be trusted!
: For the last time, Rika- that was not my car. That was my neighbor’s car. And I cannot give you permission to use other people’s things.
: We were all so foolish back then.
: To think we could have just...put a stop to it, but...
: You know, when you’re that young, it’s hard to see five feet in front of you.
: And it’s even harder when there’s a thirty foot ball right there blocking your line of sight.
: I would have let you drive my neighbor’s car! I give so much and get so little!
: Isn’t this kind of dangerous? That thing looks like it could crush us.
: Only the weak are crushed. True champions rise above the challenge and grab life by its oversized balls.
: Yeah, I don’t care how strong you are, you are not grabbing life by that.
: I want to climb it.
: You seemed to enjoy death ball more than the rest of your classmates. Why was that?
: There was just something about it, you know? I’d never seen a ball that huge before. And the way I see it, the bigger the balls, the more fun I’m going to have when all is said and done.
: Cut. Can we get a retake there, Uta? I’ve had to warn some of the other girls, but this docuseries isn’t for mature audiences, so we can’t have you saying things like...what was it again?
: ...The bigger the balls, the more fun I’m going to have when all is said and done?
: Yeah. Please don’t say things like that anymore.
: I didn’t mean it like that, though.
: Like, I love death ball. Don’t get me wrong. But I’ve never had that sort of relationship with it. I mean...the death ball wasn’t built for love. It was built to destroy.
: The death ball was built to destroy...
: It was built to destroy.
: How about this?! Since we can’t decide on the rules, we’ll let you girls figure everything out on your own.
: Imani, I’m not sure if I’m okay with my daughter handling balls this huge yet. She’s still in high school.
: Don’t try to tell me what balls I can and can’t handle, Mom!
: But also, yeah. I would like to go home now.
: Too bad! The contestants have already been locked in and our viewers are expecting a show! So either you leave your friends to die, or all of you die together!
: Would you say you were prepared to die back then?
: No! Absolutely not! None of us were!
: Well...except for Uta. I still don’t fully understand her relationship with the death ball.
: She assured us earlier that it was never romantic. But she acknowledged how it might have looked like that to all of you.
: Getting some reassurance after all these years is great. But there’s still so much about that day I don’t understand.
: Would you say it was the hardest thing you’ve ever had to endure?
: It was the hardest thing any one of us had to endure. And anyone who tells you otherwise is lying.
: It wasn’t that bad.
: You know, I think the craziest part of that whole ordeal was just how...unorganized it was. None of us had any idea what we were doing.
: Can you elaborate on that a little more, please?
: I work with kids a lot nowadays. And there are things you just...can’t do with them.
: For example, rolling out a thirty foot ball and telling them to just “go” would land you in hot water nowadays.
: But back then...everyone got away with everything. And if we had any amount of direction at all...maybe things wouldn’t have ended up the way they did.
: At least you can be thankful you all managed to make it out alive.
: Yeah...we’re all alive.
: But I think all of us would still tell you that some part of us died that day...
: It really wasn’t that bad.
Except it was...
That day would live on in infamy after what was meant to be a fun-filled event turned into something much more sinister.
The property damages alone would come out to be over 3,000,000,000 yen. And, combined with the death toll, it quickly became the most devastating event in Kumon-mi since the volcano eruption of 1912.
But, if it was so deadly, why isn’t it talked about today?
: Can you tell us a little more about what your strategy was once the game began?
: At first, we thought it would be a good idea to try and gain control of the ball.
: But it wasn’t until we realized that the ball had a mind of its own that we had to figure something else out.
: It had a mind of its own?
: That’s what I’ve always believed, at least. I can’t think of any other explanation as to why nothing we did worked.
: We were like cornered animals out there...like prey. It could smell our fear. And it did everything in its power to take advantage of that.
: If you could go back to that day and change one thing about your strategy, what would it be?
: I would never go back to that day. Not even hypothetically.
: I keep trying to put a reunion game together, but the only one who’s agreed to it is Tsunecchi. And it’s not like any of the girls who didn’t play would ever agree. Not after what they saw.
: How do you think it looked from an outsider’s point of view?
: It’s hard to say. But personally, I think everybody’s being a little over-dramatic.
: RUN FOR YOUR LIVES! WE’RE ALL GOING TO DIE!
: Bow before me, mortals! I am Rin, queen of the death ball! And I am here to claim your lives!
: How did you even get up there?! Weren’t you being crushed by it a second ago?!
: Yumi freed me! We’re in love and you should be jealous!
: No we’re not and no she shouldn’t! I’m just trying to win the fuckin’ game!
: Green Onion, Succubus! Stand aside! I will cut down the death ball and obtain its core to use as an ingredient in soup!
: HOW AM I SUPPOSED TO STAND ASIDE WHEN I DON’T EVEN KNOW WHAT DIRECTION I’M GOING IN?!
: Imani! What have you done now?! The entire field is on fire!
: It was Rika! All of this was her idea! I told her she was going too far but she wouldn’t listen!
: Stop throwing me under the death ball! I mean death bus! I mean bus! This is one of the very few occasions where I am completely innocent!
: Nuh-uh! You touched it last!
: Aaaah fuck! I did, didn’t I?!
: Rin! Your not-mom is coming to save you from the giant ball and the fire and stuff! But not because she loves you or anything! You just happen to be the first of six girls who-
: Sorry, can’t hear you! Don’t know you! Killing all of my friends!
: Not if I kill them first! Denizens of floor two, fall back!
: If you had to choose one girl who contributed the most to ending that chaotic first game of death ball, who would it be?
: Oh, Tsuneyo. It’s not even close.
: It would have to be Tsuneyo, right? She’s the only one who made any difference at all. The rest of us were only there as sacrifices.
: Every single one of us owes our life to her.
: Like, I don’t even want to think about what would have happened if a different class played this game.
: What was it that made Tsuneyo’s contribution to the game so special exactly?
: Probably the part where she picked the ball up and threw it into space.
: Space?
: Well, maybe not space. But definitely into the sky.
: Some say it’s still up there today.
: I’m just a normal girl with normal hobbies.

: A great deal of the footage from that event has been scrubbed from existence, but we were able to recover a photo of you holding the death ball over your head just seconds before you threw it into space.
: No, I will not sign an autograph for you.
: That’s fine. What I was going to say is that we had a team of researchers estimate the weight of the ball based on that photograph, and their estimation came out to be nearly 2,000lbs.
: That is nothing. I could have lifted two if I was born with larger arms.
: I guess the question now is...where do you draw all of that strength from? And why did you wait so long to get rid of the ball?
: That is two questions.
: You can answer them in order.
: I suppose my strength would have to come from my husband.
: Your husband?
: He’s a wonderful man who treats me very well. And I could not imagine a life without him.
: But you weren’t married when you played that game of death ball. Where did your strength come from then?
: Who says we were not already married?
: Perhaps it was just a secret back then?
: But, in regard to why I did not get rid of the ball earlier...
: I don’t know.
: Maybe I just didn’t know where to put it?
Floor 1: 4\nFloor 2: 3
